transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-07 16:00 PDT / Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Meridian CTO), Lena Ortiz (Meridian ML Eng), Priya Desai (Meridian Head of Infra)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Maya and Diego from our Optimize and infra team. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Samir: Good, thanks. Quick heads-up, we're on Pacific, trying to keep this tight, we have 55 minutes.
00:12 Maya: Great, we'll run through high-level then dig into INT8/FP8 profiles and quality vs latency charts, save time for questions and next steps.
00:20 Lena: Sounds good. We're most interested in chat latency at p99 and quality for our summarization prompts.
00:25 Priya: And I'll focus on deployment options - private vs dedicated, encryption, KMS, VPC peering notes.

02:10 Jordan: Quick context - Meridian's current stack? Samir, can you summarize?
02:16 Samir: Sure. We're using a mix of in-house models for retrieval, but production chat uses a 13B open model on AWS instances, mostly A100s, with some spikes on G5 in the past; response time has been variable, cost is high, and we're seeing regressive quality when we tried 4-bit in-house quantization.
02:37 Jordan: Got it, that's common. The Optimize walkthrough today will focus on our curated quantization profiles. We'll show results we see with INT8 and FP8 on comparable models and how Redwood's runtime preserves KV cache semantics and reduces quality regressions.

05:05 Maya: Ok here's the meat - INT8 profiles give the best throughput and cost savings, usually 2-4x token throughput improvement vs FP16, but can introduce quality drift depending on model and prompt type. FP8 is a newer middle ground: better fidelity than INT8 with less throughput than pure FP16 but still substantial cost savings.
05:30 Lena: When you say quality drift, can you quantify? Like accuracy or F1 drop for generation tasks?
05:38 Maya: Good question. It depends on task. For open-ended summarization we typically see BLEU/ROUGE-ish style deltas - small but perceptible. In our internal benchmarks on a 13B LLM with a curated prompt set, INT8 had about a 2-6% drop on semantic similarity metrics, whereas FP8 was 0.5-2% - varies per prompt.
05:59 Diego: Also it's not uniform across layers; some attention layers are more sensitive, so our profiles selectively keep critical layers in higher precision. That's why we call them profiles rather than blunt quantization.

10:12 Samir: Do you have real latency numbers? Our target is sub-300ms p95 for short chat turns.
10:20 Maya: Yes. On an xGPU box with optimized kernels, FP8 tends to add ~15-40ms compared to INT8 which is faster; p50 improvements can be substantial - for example, INT8 on our bench gave p50 ~60ms and p95 ~180ms for 13B-ish sequences at short context, while FP8 was p50 ~85ms p95 ~210ms. These are approximate and depend on batching and prefix caching.

13:45 Priya: For our infra, we care about deterministic tail latency. How do the fallbacks work if INT8 causes a failed request or regression?
13:52 Diego: Redwood routes by policy - we can fallback to a FP8 or FP16 variant automatically if quality monitors flag regressions or if p99 latency exceeds threshold. That routing can be regional or per-customer. Also you can pin a rollout to a small % of traffic for canary.

18:20 Lena: We saw in the past that our in-house 4-bit attempt had hallucinations on certain legal prompts. What's the chance of hallucination increase with INT8?
18:29 Maya: Hallucinations are tricky - usually quantization affects token probabilities and can slightly increase nonsensical token probability in edge cases. Our eval harness runs semantic consistency checks and targeted prompts to catch those. For production we recommend a two-stage approach: run INT8/FP8 in shadow mode for a week on a representative traffic slice and run automatic regression checks on NLI/consistency prompts.

22:00 Samir: On security, can you confirm data never leaves our VPC for Private? We need KMS/HSM support and audit logs for compliance.
22:10 Jordan: For Redwood Private, the control plane can be customer-managed and all inference traffic stays in your VPC. We integrate with KMS; HSM is supported for Enterprise packages. We also expose audit logs and per-request trace IDs. We'll share SOC2 and SOC3 artifacts in the doc pack.

26:03 Priya: Network egress latency is a concern. If we use Dedicated, is there a latency penalty?
26:10 Diego: Dedicated pools are co-located and you can choose region; latency is typically lower because there's no multi-tenant scheduler. Private on-prem can be lowest but depends on your network and GPUs. We'll include a recommended config for low-p99 latency.

30:05 Maya: I'll pull up the benchmark slide - (shared link: /redwood/benchmarks/meridian-13b-int8-fp8-2026-03-07.xlsx). Key takeaways: INT8 best for throughput/cost, FP8 better for quality-sensitive prompts. We include per-prompt delta and per-layer sensitivity heatmaps.
30:40 Lena: Can you share that sheet after?
30:45 Jordan: Absolutely - we'll send it.

33:50 Samir: Cost modelling - what's the delta in $/million tokens?
33:56 Jordan: Rough ballpark: INT8 can reduce cost per token by ~40-60% vs FP16 baseline depending on hardware; FP8 sits around 25-40% savings. We'll provide a detailed cost model using your traffic profile.

37:25 Maya: For rollout, recommended path: 1) create a canary with 1-5% traffic on INT8 with logging enabled, 2) run automatic regressions and human-in-the-loop review for two weeks, 3) broaden rollout if metrics stable, 4) enable auto-fallback to FP8/FP16 on rule triggers.

40:10 Priya: What's required from our side for a POC?
40:15 Jordan: Typically we ask for a 10k prompt slice, a sample dataset for eval, infra specs, and an SSO user for engineers. We'll run bench jobs and share the spreadsheet. That gets us concrete numbers.

43:00 Lena: Who will own the eval scripts? Do you provide them?
43:05 Maya: We supply the eval harness and scripts; you can run locally or we can run in a Private deployment. For Dedicated we can run on our infra and share results.

47:30 Samir: Anything else on model variants? Can we pin specific model versions?
47:36 Diego: Yes you can pin model versions and quantization profiles per route. Our console exposes rollouts and per-route dashboards. We'll demo the console in the POC scoping call.

50:00 Jordan: Recap - we'll send: benchmark spreadsheet, pricing/cost model, SOC2 docs, POC scoping invite. Action items listed in the doc.
50:12 Samir: Good. Let's get the POC scoped, Priya will share infra details.
50:20 Priya: I'll add Diego and Maya to our infra Slack channel and share network docs.

54:00 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the POC scoping.
54:10 Lena: Thanks all.
54:12 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional proper nouns misheard (Meridain spelled as Meridain/Meridian), timestamps approximate, speaker labels from calendar and Fireflies auto-attribution.
